routes.description: Establish that contemporary cosmology supports neutral premises concerning a finite cosmic past and fine-tuned initial conditions, then connect those premises through causal and design reasoning to a transcendent personal creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if cosmological evidence makes a beginning and purposive fine-tuning sufficiently credible, naturalistic alternatives do not remove their explanatory force, and the resulting causal and design inferences make God's existence more probable.

motionBridge.description: Show that the relevant cosmological evidence raises the probability of a transcendent creator and designer.

centralBridges.description: Establish that expansion, thermodynamics, and the limits of proposed eternal models favor an ultimate cosmic beginning.
Establish that a universe beginning to exist requires a cause beyond physical spacetime and that personal agency can account for a finite effect.
Establish that life-permitting constants and low initial entropy are improbable without design and are more expected under theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify theoretical, thermodynamic, and observer-typicality difficulties confronting beginningless or multiverse alternatives.
Maintain the distinction between cosmology supplying neutral premises and philosophical arguments drawing the theistic conclusion.

routes.description: Establish that self-contained naturalistic cosmological models can account for a finite or eternal universe, while theistic explanations lack constrained observational expectations and add no required explanatory element.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if neither a cosmic boundary nor fine-tuning requires a transcendent agent, viable naturalistic models remain available, and comparative explanatory standards favor constrained, self-contained accounts over an underdetermined theistic explanation.

motionBridge.description: Show that naturalistic cosmological models explain the universe without making God's existence more probable.

centralBridges.description: Establish that singularity results do not prove an absolute beginning and that coherent finite or eternal models need no external cause.
Establish that causal concepts grounded within spacetime need not apply to the universe as a whole or to a first temporal boundary.
Establish that fine-tuning probabilities are measure-dependent and that naturalistic principles or multiverse models can address observed conditions.
Require competing explanations to generate constrained expectations and show how self-contained naturalism can meet that requirement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Treat low entropy and observer typicality as model-dependent research problems rather than direct evidence of divine design.
Apply parsimony and explanatory self-containment when an invisible creator adds no distinct observational consequences.

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning and Eternal Models
sections.rationale: Whether contemporary expansion results, singularity theorems, thermodynamics, and quantum cosmologies favor an ultimate beginning is a principal empirical premise in the cosmological argument.

sections.title: Causation, Time, and a First Moment
sections.rationale: The inference from a temporal boundary to a transcendent personal cause depends on whether causation applies to the universe and how temporal becoming and first moments are understood.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning and Cosmological Probability
sections.rationale: The design inference requires defensible probability measures, genuinely restricted life-permitting conditions, and a justified comparison of those observations under theism and naturalism.

sections.title: Low Entropy, Multiverses, and Observer Typicality
sections.rationale: Low initial entropy and the prevalence of ordinary observers test whether multiverse or equilibrium models provide an adequate naturalistic alternative to purposive design.

sections.title: Explanatory Scope and Predictive Standards
sections.rationale: The motion-level comparison depends on whether theism functions as an evidential conclusion from neutral premises and whether either worldview supplies constrained, parsimonious observational expectations.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Contemporary cosmology provides evidence for religiously neutral premises in philosophical arguments whose conclusions have theological significance.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Expansion evidence and the limits of classical and quantum cosmological regimes make it more likely than not that the universe began to exist.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: The second law of thermodynamics supports a temporal beginning, while eternal fluctuation cosmologies face unitarity, generalized-second-law, and Boltzmann-brain problems.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Cosmic fine-tuning is better explained by design because physical necessity lacks support and chance-based multiverse accounts make ordinary embodied observers comparatively improbable.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Low initial entropy is genuine fine-tuning that multiverse models do not adequately explain, whereas theism can connect it to an orderly and scientifically discoverable creation.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: God is not proposed as a scientific theory competing with cosmological models; those models instead support neutral premises from which philosophical arguments infer a creator and designer.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Whatever begins to exist requires a cause because being cannot arise from nonbeing, uncaused emergence would not discriminate among possible objects, and experience supports causation.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: A multiverse does not resolve observer typicality because de Sitter descendants and regions unsuitable for ordinary life can still produce Boltzmann brains without ordinary observers.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: A cause need not temporally precede its effect: creation can coincide with the universe's first moment, with God timeless without creation and temporal from creation onward.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-09.proposition: Fine-tuning probabilities can be assessed across a conceptual space of possible constants and quantities without requiring multiple universes to exist in actuality.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Modern physics does not require a transcendent cause, because a complete mathematical cosmological model can describe a universe with a beginning without positing anything external.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Whether the universe is eternal must be decided through viable cosmological models, and neither abstract beginning principles nor the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin result establishes a universally finite past.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: The early universe's unexplained low entropy is an open cosmological problem rather than evidence for God, and a naturalistic boundary principle or non-equilibrium eternal model may explain it.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Carroll's eternal model remains coherent because its evolution is unitary, a cited baby-universe statement concerns black holes rather than cosmology, and its thermodynamic minimum is not a temporal beginning.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Sensitivity of familiar local conditions to changes in physical parameters does not establish that every form of life or information processing would be impossible under different conditions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Alleged fine-tuning can disappear under rigorous physical analysis, as the supposedly improbable early expansion rate is generic rather than exceptional under the relevant general-relativistic measure.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: A multiverse can follow from a simple physical theory, generate probabilistic predictions, and avoid domination by Boltzmann brains in viable models whose observer ratios are empirically discriminating.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Theism lacks predictive force when flexible post hoc explanations can accommodate observations that repeatedly resemble naturalistic expectations rather than distinctive expectations generated by divine design.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Causal language grounded in laws, temporal order, and the thermodynamic arrow within the universe does not justify demanding an external cause for the universe or total reality as a whole.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-06.proposition: Although an invisible creator remains logically conceivable, a naturalistic model that fits the observations with fewer additions and greater self-containment is explanatorily preferable by ordinary scientific and philosophical standards.
